member.name: T:Voltaic.A2A.A2ACallerContext
member.summary:
Internal, request-scoped bridge that carries the authenticated caller's from a server's authentication site to the point where the handed to the agent handler is constructed.
The A2A gRPC server delegates to the A2A HTTP endpoint's public methods, so the authenticated identity cannot be threaded through as a parameter without changing that public surface. This flows the caller along the shared asynchronous request flow instead; the constructed copies the identity onto itself so it survives into the background handler task and the streaming loop, where the ambient scope no longer applies.

member.name: P:Voltaic.A2A.A2ACallerContext.Current
member.summary: Gets the authenticated caller for the current request flow, or null when unauthenticated.

member.name: M:Voltaic.A2A.A2ACallerContext.Push(Voltaic.Core.AuthenticationResult)
member.summary: Makes the supplied authenticated caller ambient for the current asynchronous flow and returns a token that restores the prior value when disposed. Pushing null is a safe no-op-then-restore for unauthenticated request paths.
member.param: The authenticated caller, or null.
member.returns: An that restores the previously ambient value when disposed.

member.name: T:Voltaic.A2A.A2AGrpcServer
member.summary:
Direct A2A gRPC server for the lf.a2a.v1.A2AService service, hosted on WatsonWebserver with HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and cleartext HTTP/2 (h2c) enabled, using gRPC length-prefixed protobuf framing.
gRPC calls are POST requests under /lf.a2a.v1.A2AService/ and require HTTP/2 (other protocols get HTTP 426). When is true, GET and GET are also served as JSON. Task state, push notification configurations, and handler execution are shared with an internal (which is never started), so results match the JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON bindings.
Security: requests are gated in order by (on by default for a loopback host name), , and , as on . Only the public Agent Card is served without authentication. Errors other than A2A protocol errors are reported to clients as a generic grpc-message, and the details are logged through . A host name of * or + listens on all interfaces (0.0.0.0, plus :: when IPv6 is available).
Loopback: a host name of localhost listens on both 127.0.0.1 and ::1 (the IPv6 listener is best effort and skipped when it cannot bind). Clients such as resolve localhost to ::1 first; without an IPv6 listener each new connection would wait for the refused IPv6 attempt (about two seconds on Windows) before falling back to IPv4. An explicit address such as 127.0.0.1 listens on that address only, so clients should connect to that same address.
Configure properties and register the handler before calling . Requests are handled concurrently; the public members are not synchronized against concurrent reconfiguration.

When it returns false, the server responds with and (or Unauthorized) as text/plain, plus (for example WWW-Authenticate). On success, and are copied onto the the agent handler receives. member.name: T:Voltaic.A2A.A2AHttpServer
member.summary: Hosts an A2A v1.0 agent over HTTP: the public Agent Card at , the extended Agent Card at , the JSON-RPC binding at the RPC path (default /a2a), the HTTP+JSON (REST) binding, and SSE streaming for streaming methods. Requests are gated in order by , , CORS preflight handling, and . When the Agent Card advertises push notifications, every task event is delivered to the task's registered webhooks (see , , and ). JSON-RPC errors are returned with HTTP 200 and a JSON-RPC error body; HTTP+JSON errors use the A2A status mapping. Requests are handled concurrently; configure properties before calling . The operation methods (for example ) are the same ones the HTTP bindings call and can also be invoked in-process.

member.name: P:Voltaic.A2A.A2AHttpServer.AgentCard
member.summary: Gets or sets the public Agent Card, served without authentication at . Its capabilities also gate server behavior: push notification methods require pushNotifications, and the extended card requires extendedAgentCard. Set in the constructor; should not be set to null.

member.name: P:Voltaic.A2A.A2AHttpServer.ExtendedAgentCard
member.summary: Gets or sets the extended Agent Card, returned by GetExtendedAgentCard and to authenticated callers when advertises capabilities.extendedAgentCard. Default is null, which returns when the capability is advertised.

member.name: P:Voltaic.A2A.A2AHttpServer.Handler
member.summary: Gets the agent handler that processes messages. Null until one is passed to the constructor or ; message and cancel requests fail with while it is null.

member.name: P:Voltaic.A2A.A2AHttpServer.AuthenticationHandler
member.summary: Gets or sets an optional asynchronous authentication handler. When set, every request that passes the loopback and origin checks, except CORS preflight (OPTIONS) and GET of the public Agent Card, is passed to it. On failure the server returns the result's , (for example WWW-Authenticate), and (default text Unauthorized). On success the result's and are copied onto . Default is null, which performs no authentication; the loopback and origin checks still apply.

member.name: P:Voltaic.A2A.A2AHttpServer.EnableCors
member.summary: Gets or sets whether CORS headers are sent. When enabled, a request from a browser origin that allows receives Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to that origin (never *), Vary: Origin, and the . Requests without an Origin header receive no CORS headers. Origins the policy rejects get HTTP 403 whether CORS is on or off. Default is true.

member.name: P:Voltaic.A2A.A2AHttpServer.CorsHeaders
member.summary: Gets or sets additional CORS headers sent to allowed browser origins when is true. An Access-Control-Allow-Origin or Vary entry is ignored, because the allowed origin is always echoed; use to choose origins.

member.name: P:Voltaic.A2A.A2AHttpServer.OriginPolicy
member.summary: Gets or sets the policy that decides which browser origins may call the server. A request whose Origin the policy rejects receives HTTP 403 with no CORS headers, before preflight handling and authentication, including requests for the public Agent Card. The default allows requests without an Origin header and loopback origins. Setting null restores the default policy.

member.name: P:Voltaic.A2A.A2AHttpServer.RestrictToLoopbackClients
member.summary: Gets or sets whether only loopback clients are served. When true, a request whose remote address is not loopback receives HTTP 403. Default is true when the server is constructed with a loopback host name (localhost, 127.x.x.x, or ::1) and false otherwise. On Windows a localhost prefix is served on every interface and routed by the spoofable Host header, so this check is what keeps such a server local.

member.name: P:Voltaic.A2A.A2AHttpServer.PushNotificationUrlValidator
member.summary: Gets or sets an optional validator for push notification webhook URLs, which replaces the built-in server-side request forgery (SSRF) protection. When null (the default), a webhook URL must be absolute http or https without user information, must not name localhost or a loopback, private, link-local, carrier-grade NAT, or multicast IP literal, and is re-checked when the server connects: if the host name resolves only to such addresses, delivery is refused (this also defeats DNS rebinding). Redirects are never followed and no proxy is used. When set, the delegate alone decides: return true to allow the URL (for example, an allowlist of webhook hosts, or loopback during local development); connect-time address checks are then skipped. A URL that fails validation is rejected with when the configuration is created.

member.name: P:Voltaic.A2A.A2AHttpServer.PushNotificationTimeoutMs
member.summary: Gets or sets the timeout for each push notification request, in milliseconds. Default is 10000 (the A2A specification recommends 10 to 30 seconds). Minimum 1000, maximum 300000.
member.exception: Thrown when the value is outside 1000 to 300000.

member.name: P:Voltaic.A2A.A2AHttpServer.PushNotificationMaxAttempts
member.summary: Gets or sets how many times a push notification is attempted before it is dropped. Failed attempts (a non-2xx response, a timeout, or a connection error) are retried with exponential backoff starting at 500 milliseconds. Default is 3. Minimum 1, maximum 10.
member.exception: Thrown when the value is outside 1 to 10.

member.name: T:Voltaic.Core.AuthenticationResult
member.summary: Represents the result of an HTTP authentication attempt. When is false, the server returns the specified and to the client without processing the request further. When is true, optional identity information such as and can be carried forward for use in downstream tool handlers.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Core.AuthenticationResult.IsAuthenticated
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the request was successfully authenticated. When false, the server will reject the request with the configured and .

member.name: P:Voltaic.Core.AuthenticationResult.Principal
member.summary: Gets or sets the authenticated principal name (e.g., username, service account, API key identifier). This value is informational and can be used by tool handlers to determine who is calling. Default is null, indicating no principal information is available.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Core.AuthenticationResult.Claims
member.summary: Gets or sets additional claims or metadata associated with the authenticated identity. Tool handlers can use these claims for fine-grained authorization decisions. Default is null, indicating no additional claims are available.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Core.AuthenticationResult.StatusCode
member.summary: Gets or sets the HTTP status code to return when authentication fails. Common values are 401 (Unauthorized) and 403 (Forbidden). Default is 401. Only used when is false.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Core.AuthenticationResult.ErrorMessage
member.summary: Gets or sets the error message to include in the response body when authentication fails. Default is null, which results in no response body being sent. Only used when is false.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Core.AuthenticationResult.Headers
member.summary: Gets or sets headers to add to the response when authentication fails, for example WWW-Authenticate (required on a 401 by RFC 6750 and the MCP authorization specification) or Retry-After. Names are case-insensitive. Ignored when is true. Never null; setting null stores an empty dictionary. HTTP and WebSocket servers write these headers on the rejection; the A2A gRPC server does not.

member.name: M:Voltaic.Core.AuthenticationResult.BearerChallenge(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Creates a failed result for bearer-token authentication: status 401 and a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer challenge in the RFC 6750 format, for example Bearer resource_metadata="https://api.example/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource", error="invalid_token". Parameter values are quoted, and embedded quotes and backslashes are escaped.
member.param: Optional protected resource metadata URL (RFC 9728), which MCP clients use to discover the authorization server. Null or empty omits it.
Optional RFC 6750 error code, such as invalid_token or insufficient_scope. Null or empty omits it.
Optional human-readable error description. Null or empty omits it.
Optional response body text. Null sends no body.
member.returns: A failed authentication result carrying the challenge header.

member.name: M:Voltaic.Core.AuthenticationResult.BearerChallenge(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Creates a failed result for bearer-token authentication with a scope parameter: status 401 and a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer challenge naming the scopes a token needs, as the MCP authorization specification (2025-11-25) recommends so clients can request them.
member.param: Optional protected resource metadata URL (RFC 9728). Null or empty omits it.
Optional RFC 6750 error code. Null or empty omits it.
Optional human-readable error description. Null or empty omits it.
Optional response body text. Null sends no body.
Space-separated scopes the resource requires. Null or empty omits it.
member.returns: A failed authentication result carrying the challenge header.

member.name: M:Voltaic.Core.AuthenticationResult.InsufficientScope(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Creates a failed result for a valid token that lacks a required scope: status 403 and WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="..." (RFC 6750 section 3.1), as the MCP authorization specification recommends, so the client can obtain a token with the scope. To reject a single tool call instead of a whole request, throw McpInsufficientScopeException from the handler.
member.param: Space-separated scopes required. Must not be null or whitespace.
Optional protected resource metadata URL (RFC 9728). Null or empty omits it.
Optional human-readable description. Null or empty omits it.
Optional response body text. Null sends no body.
member.returns: A failed authentication result with status 403.
member.exception: Thrown when is null or whitespace.

member.summary: Represents a connected client with its associated resources and metadata. Supports multiple connection types: TCP, WebSocket, HTTP, and Stdio.

member.summary: Gets the type of client connection.

member.summary: Gets the unique identifier or session ID for this client connection.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Core.ClientConnection.Caller
member.summary: Gets or sets the authenticated caller that opened this connection, or null when the server has no authentication handler (or the connection is not authenticated). sets it from the upgrade request's and makes it the ambient for every request on the socket. sets it when a session is created and rejects later requests on that session from a different principal.

member.summary: Gets the timestamp of the last activity on this connection. Updated when notifications are enqueued or dequeued.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Core.ClientConnection.MaxQueueSize
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of notifications that can be queued. When the limit is reached, oldest notifications are discarded. Default is 100 notifications. Minimum is 1.

member.summary: Gets the underlying TCP client. Only applicable for TCP connection types.

member.summary: Gets the cancellation token source for this connection.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Core.ClientConnection.WriteLock
member.summary: Gets the lock that serializes writes to this connection, so concurrent responses never interleave.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Core.ClientConnection.NewlineFraming
member.summary: Gets or sets whether this TCP connection uses newline-delimited framing instead of Content-Length framing.

member.summary: Gets or sets protocol state a server keeps for this connection (for example the MCP session state).

member.name: M:Voltaic.Core.ClientConnection.DequeueAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)

member.name: M:Voltaic.Core.ClientConnection.MarkActivity

member.summary: Registers the handler for requests the server sends to this client with the given method name, replacing any previous handler for that method. The handler receives the request parameters (null when the request has none) and a token that is cancelled when the client disconnects; its return value is sent as the result (null is sent as an empty object). member.name: T:Voltaic.Core.MessageFraming
member.summary: Provides LSP-style message framing for JSON-RPC 2.0 messages. Messages are formatted as: Content-Length: {size}\r\n\r\n{json_body} The reader accepts only the LSP header grammar: every header line must be Content-Length (exactly once, digits only) or Content-Type, and the complete header block may not exceed 1024 bytes. Anything else, including an HTTP request line or HTTP headers such as Host or Origin, raises and the connection is closed, so a web page cannot drive a TCP server with a cross-protocol fetch().

member.name: T:Voltaic.Core.OriginPolicy
member.summary:
Decides which browser origins may call an HTTP or WebSocket server. The MCP Streamable HTTP specification requires servers to validate the Origin header on every request to prevent DNS rebinding and cross-site requests, so this policy applies whether or not authentication is configured.
The default policy allows requests without an Origin header (non-browser clients such as SDKs, curl, and other servers) and requests from loopback origins (http(s)://localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, and [::1] on any port). Every other origin is rejected with HTTP 403 unless it is listed in .
Configure the policy before the server starts. Reads are thread-safe; changing the policy while the server is handling requests is not synchronized.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Core.OriginPolicy.AllowedOrigins
member.summary: Gets or sets browser origins allowed in addition to loopback origins, for example https://app.example.com or http://intranet.local:8080. Matching compares scheme, host, and port case-insensitively, and treats a default port (80 for http, 443 for https) as equal to an omitted port. The entry * allows every origin, which is not recommended because it re-enables cross-site and DNS rebinding access. Default is empty. Setting null stores an empty list.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Core.OriginPolicy.AllowLoopbackOrigins
member.summary: Gets or sets whether loopback origins (http(s)://localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, and [::1] on any port) are always allowed. Default is true, so local browser tools such as the MCP Inspector keep working.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Core.OriginPolicy.OriginValidator
member.summary: Gets or sets an optional validator that replaces the built-in rules. It receives the raw Origin header value, or null when the request has none, and returns true to allow the request. Default is null, which uses and . Exceptions thrown by the validator are treated as a rejection.

member.name: M:Voltaic.Core.OriginPolicy.IsAllowed(System.String)
member.summary: Returns true when a request carrying may be served. A null origin (the header is absent) is allowed unless says otherwise. An empty or malformed origin, including the literal null sent by sandboxed pages and file: documents, is rejected unless listed or allowed by the validator.
member.param: The Origin header value, or null when absent.
member.returns: True when the request is allowed; otherwise false.

member.name: M:Voltaic.Core.OriginPolicy.IsLoopbackOrigin(System.String)
member.summary: Returns true when is an http or https origin whose host is localhost, a 127.0.0.0/8 address, or [::1]. Lookalikes such as http://localhost.evil.example or http://127.0.0.1.evil.example are not loopback.
member.param: The origin to test. May be null.
member.returns: True for loopback origins; otherwise false.

member.name: T:Voltaic.Core.RpcCallContext
member.summary:
Ambient, request-scoped context describing the authenticated caller for the JSON-RPC / MCP request currently being handled on this asynchronous flow.
The context is populated by the transport immediately after a successful and restored to its prior value when the request completes. Because it is stored in an , it flows automatically through the awaited call chain into method and tool handlers without any change to their signatures, and concurrent requests on independent asynchronous flows never observe one another's context.
Handlers read to authorize per-caller (for example, to scope reads or gate writes by tenant, user, or role). is when no authentication handler is configured on the transport, when the transport does not support authentication, or when the request was allowed to bypass authentication (for example, the MCP ping handshake).
member.remarks: This type is immutable and therefore thread-safe. The ambient value is isolated per asynchronous flow by ; reads from on unrelated flows are safe and independent.

member.summary: Gets the context for the request currently being handled on this asynchronous flow, or when there is no authenticated caller for the current request.

member.name: M:Voltaic.Mcp.McpClient.RegisterRequestHandler(System.String,System.Func{Voltaic.Core.RpcParameters,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Threading.Tasks.Task{System.Object}})
member.summary: Registers the handler for requests the server sends to this client with the given method name (for example roots/list, sampling/createMessage, or elicitation/create), replacing any previous handler for that method. The handler receives the request parameters (null when the request has none) and a token that is cancelled when the client shuts down; its return value is sent as the result (null is sent as an empty object). A handler that throws sends that error; any other exception sends -32603 without its message. Requests for methods without a handler are answered with -32601. ping is always answered by the client itself. Handlers run concurrently with each other and with the receive loop. Thread-safe.
member.param: The method name, compared case-sensitively. Must not be null, empty, or whitespace, and must not be ping.
The handler. Must not be null.
member.exception: Thrown when is null, empty, or whitespace, or is null.
Thrown when is ping.

member.name: T:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpClient
member.summary:
Provides an HTTP-based MCP (Model Context Protocol) client implementation. Supports JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP with Server-Sent Events (SSE) for server-to-client messages.
Requests the server sends to the client over a session (on the GET stream or on a POST response stream) are always answered by POSTing the JSON-RPC response back to the endpoint: ping with an empty result ({}), as the MCP specification requires of both parties, other methods by handlers registered with , and anything else with -32601 (method not found). The stateless 2026-07-28 revision forbids server requests on streams (servers use Multi Round-Trip Requests instead), so they are logged and ignored in stateless mode.
SSE streams are parsed per the event stream rules: event IDs are tracked, empty priming events are skipped, and a stream the server closes is reopened (when is true) with Last-Event-ID after the server's retry interval or . A POST response stream that ends before its response is resumed the same way with a GET request.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpClient.SessionId
member.summary: Gets the session ID assigned by the server. This ID is used to correlate requests and receive notifications via SSE.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpClient.IsConnected
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the client is currently connected to a server. A client is considered connected if it has a valid session ID.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpClient.IsSseConnected

member.summary: Returns the JSON-RPC response body for a request. Streamable HTTP servers may answer a POST with either application/json or an SSE stream (text/event-stream) that carries notifications, server requests, and then the response; the specification requires clients to support both. For a stream, events are read as they arrive: notifications are raised through , server requests are answered, and reading stops at the response whose id matches . When the stream ends early after an event ID, it is resumed with GET and Last-Event-ID (handshake era only). Returns an empty string when no response arrives.

member.name: T:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpResponseWriter
member.summary: Writes the response to one Streamable HTTP POST. It stays a single JSON response unless something must be sent before the result (a notification related to the request, or a keep-alive), in which case it becomes an SSE stream (text/event-stream) that ends with the JSON-RPC response. On a session, the stream is resumable: every event carries an ID and is logged, a priming event (an ID with empty data) comes first where the session's revision asks for one, and a client that loses the connection can resume with GET and Last-Event-ID; events keep being logged after the connection breaks. Thread-safe.

member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of notifications that can be queued per client connection. When the limit is reached, oldest notifications are discarded. Default is 100 notifications. Minimum is 1. This value is applied to new client connections when they are established.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpServer.ResponseKeepAliveMs
member.summary: Gets or sets how long a stateless (2026-07-28) request may run silently before its response turns into an SSE stream that carries a keep-alive comment every interval, so a client that closed the stream (which that revision defines as cancellation) is noticed, and the request cancelled, while the handler runs: detects a closed connection only by writing to it. A response that completes within the interval keeps its exact HTTP status (for example 400 for -32021); once the first keep-alive is sent the status is 200 and a later error arrives as the final SSE event. Default is 15000. 0 disables keep-alives, so a closed stream is noticed only at the next write (a progress or log notification, or the response). Minimum is 0; maximum is 600000.
member.exception: Thrown when set outside 0 to 600000.

member.summary: Gets or sets how many recent events of each resumable SSE stream on the MCP endpoint are kept for replay: GET streams and the SSE response streams of POST requests on a session. Every event on such a stream carries an ID of the form {streamId}-{sequence}; on sessions that negotiated 2025-11-25 or later each stream starts with a priming event (an ID and an empty data field), as that revision recommends. A client that reconnects with GET and Last-Event-ID receives the retained events after that ID, on the same stream; IDs from another session or an unknown stream start a new stream. Each session keeps its most recent streams. Default is 100. Minimum is 0 (IDs are still sent, but nothing is replayed); maximum is 10000.
member.exception: Thrown when set outside 0 to 10000.

Clients wait this long before reconnecting after the stream closes. Default is 1000. Minimum is 0; maximum is 600000.
member.exception: Thrown when set outside 0 to 600000.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpServer.RequireInitializedSessions
member.summary:
Obsolete; always true. Since v2.1.4 handshake-era sessions are created only by a successful initialize, as the MCP Streamable HTTP specification requires, and this setting has no effect:
A session is created, is raised, and the MCP-Session-Id header is returned only when initialize succeeds. A rejected initialize creates nothing.
A POST to the MCP endpoint without MCP-Session-Id is rejected with HTTP 400, except initialize.
A POST to the JSON-RPC endpoint without MCP-Session-Id is served on a temporary connection that is never registered, and no session header is returned.
Session IDs are always generated by the server, a request carrying an MCP-Session-Id the server does not know (never issued, expired, or terminated) is rejected with HTTP 404, and a failed request never creates a session. The stateless 2026-07-28 revision never uses sessions. Clients that opened a session with ping ( from Voltaic 2.0.0 and earlier) must be upgraded. Setting this property is ignored.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpServer.EnableCors
member.summary: Gets or sets whether CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) headers are sent. When enabled, a request from a browser origin that allows receives Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to that origin (never *), Vary: Origin, and the . Requests without an Origin header receive no CORS headers. This setting never widens access: origins the policy rejects get HTTP 403 whether CORS is on or off. Default is true.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpServer.CorsHeaders
member.summary: Additional CORS headers sent to allowed browser origins when is true. Defaults: Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, DELETE, OPTIONS, an explicit Access-Control-Allow-Headers list (including Authorization and the MCP headers; on a preflight that names the headers it wants, those names are allowed instead, so custom headers such as X-API-Key or Mcp-Param-* work), Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Mcp-Session-Id, MCP-Protocol-Version, WWW-Authenticate (so browser clients can read the session and the OAuth challenge), and Access-Control-Max-Age: 86400. An Access-Control-Allow-Origin or Vary entry is ignored, because the allowed origin is always echoed; use to choose origins. Setting null stores an empty dictionary.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpServer.OriginPolicy
member.summary: Gets or sets the policy that decides which browser origins may call the server. The MCP specification requires servers to validate Origin on every request to prevent DNS rebinding and cross-site calls. Requests whose origin the policy rejects receive HTTP 403 with no CORS headers, before routing, preflight handling, or authentication. The default allows requests without an Origin header and loopback origins; add browser origins to . Setting null restores the default policy.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpServer.ProtectedResourceMetadata
member.summary: Gets or sets the OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) document the server publishes. The MCP authorization specification requires servers that use OAuth to publish it so clients can find the authorization server. When set, a GET to the well-known URL derived from (RFC 9728 section 3.3: followed by the resource's path, for example /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp for https://host/mcp, or the bare path for a resource without one) returns the document as JSON, without calling ; the loopback and origin checks still apply. Other forms of the path are not served, because a client must reject a document whose resource does not match the URL it fetched. Every Bearer challenge the server sends that lacks resource_metadata gets that URL added, so pass null as the URL to . Default is null, which serves nothing at those paths (HTTP 404).
member.exception: Thrown when the value's is empty or not an absolute https (or http) URL without a fragment, or it has no .

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpServer.RestrictToLoopbackClients
member.summary: Gets or sets whether only loopback clients are served. When true, a request whose remote address is not loopback (127.0.0.0/8, ::1, or an IPv4-mapped loopback address) receives HTTP 403. Default is true when the server is constructed with a loopback host name (localhost, 127.x.x.x, or ::1) and false otherwise. This matters on Windows, where (http.sys) listens on every interface for a localhost prefix and routes by the Host header, which a remote client can spoof. Bind to +, *, or a specific address to serve remote clients, or set this to false explicitly.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpServer.IncludeToolExceptionMessages

A handler exception becomes a tool result with isError set to true (a tool execution error the model can read). When false (the default), the text is a generic "Tool '<name>' failed because of an internal error." so internal details (connection strings, paths, host names) are not sent, as the MCP security considerations require tool outputs to be sanitized; when true, the text is "Tool '<name>' failed: <message>". member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpServer.MaximumHandshakeProtocolVersion
member.summary: Gets or sets the newest protocol revision the server agrees to during an initialize handshake. A client that requests a newer revision, or a stateless-era revision such as 2026-07-28 (which defines no initialize request and no sessions), is answered with this value, following the MCP rule that a server responds with a version it supports. Default is (currently 2025-11-25). Lower it to pin clients to an older revision. Setting null restores the default. Set this before the server starts accepting requests; it is not synchronized with in-flight handshakes.
member.exception: Thrown when the value is not a supported handshake-era revision (for example 2026-07-28 or an unknown version).

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpServer.ProgressIntervalMs
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum interval, in milliseconds, between progress notifications sent for one request (MCP: senders should rate-limit progress). An update that follows the previous one sooner is not sent, except the final one (progress equal to the total). Default is 20. 0 sends every update. Maximum is 60000.
member.exception: Thrown when set outside 0 to 60000.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpServer.MaxResumableStreamsPerSession
member.summary: Gets or sets how many SSE streams (GET streams and POST response streams) each session keeps for resumption with Last-Event-ID. When more are opened, the oldest is forgotten and can no longer be resumed. Default is 8. Minimum is 1; maximum is 1000. Applies to sessions created afterwards.
member.exception: Thrown when set outside 1 to 1000.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpHttpServer.AuthenticationHandler
member.summary: Gets or sets an optional asynchronous authentication handler. When set, incoming HTTP requests that pass the loopback check () and origin check () are passed through this handler before processing. If the handler returns an with set to false, the server immediately returns the result's status code, (for example WWW-Authenticate), and error message without processing the request. When null (the default), no authentication is performed; requests are still subject to the loopback and origin checks. The handler receives the full so it can inspect headers, query strings, client certificates, or any other request property needed for authentication. The handler is not called for the health check endpoint (/), CORS preflight (OPTIONS), and at , so clients can check connectivity and discover the authorization server. Every other request, including ping, must authenticate, as MCP authorization requires (since v2.1.4; earlier versions answered a ping that failed authentication). Authenticated requests run through exactly the same MCP protocol pipeline as unauthenticated ones (version resolution, stateless 2026-07-28 routing, batching rules, and session tracking), so setting a handler never changes protocol behavior.

Both the MCP endpoint and the JSON-RPC endpoint call this, because server/discover advertises the stateless revision on both, so a client that chose it must get stateless results wherever it sends requests. Returns true when a response was written, including a version-resolution error; false when the request belongs to the handshake era and the caller should continue.

member.summary: Handles a POST to the MCP endpoint that resolved to the stateless (2026-07-28) era. member.name: M:Voltaic.Mcp.McpProtocol.NegotiateHandshakeVersion(System.String,System.String)
member.summary:
Negotiates the protocol version for a session-based handshake (the initialize request). A stateless-era revision cannot be negotiated through initialize, so a request for one is answered with , the newest handshake-era revision the server will speak. The rules are:
No version requested (null or blank): , lowered to the maximum when the maximum is older.
A handshake-era version at or below the maximum: that version.
A handshake-era version above the maximum: the maximum.
A stateless-era version (for example 2026-07-28): the maximum.
An unknown version: .
This method is stateless and thread-safe.
member.param: The client-requested version. May be null or blank.
The newest handshake-era version to agree to. Must be a supported handshake-era revision; see for the usual value.
member.returns: The handshake-era version to use for the session. Never null.
member.exception: Thrown when is not a supported version, or when is not a supported handshake-era revision.

member.name: T:Voltaic.Mcp.McpSchemaValidator
member.summary: Validates JSON values (tool arguments and structured tool output) against a JSON Schema, operating directly on , in the schema's declared dialect: JSON Schema 2020-12 (the default when $schema is absent) or draft-07. Both dialects: type, enum, const, properties, required, additionalProperties, patternProperties, propertyNames, minProperties, maxProperties, items, contains, minItems, maxItems, uniqueItems, minLength, maxLength, pattern (ECMA-262), minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum, multipleOf, allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, if/then/else, $ref, and boolean schemas. 2020-12 only: prefixItems, dependentRequired, dependentSchemas, minContains, maxContains, unevaluatedProperties, unevaluatedItems, $anchor, $dynamicAnchor, and $dynamicRef (dynamic scope). draft-07 only: the array form of items with additionalItems, dependencies, fragment $id anchors, and $ref overriding its sibling keywords. References resolve within the resource they appear in (a subschema with its own $id starts a resource). Another dialect, or a reference that cannot be resolved within the schema, is reported as an error rather than validated permissively. Annotation keywords (such as format, description, or x-mcp-header) are ignored, and a malformed keyword is ignored on its own without disabling the rest of the schema. Thread safety: all members are safe for concurrent use.

member.name: M:Voltaic.Mcp.McpSchemaValidator.Validate(System.Object,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Validates a value's raw JSON against a schema, throwing an validation error on the first violation. An absent value (null or blank JSON) is validated as an empty object when the schema allows objects, and is otherwise reported as required.
member.param: The schema: a , a JSON string, or any serializable object; null skips validation.
The raw JSON of the value, or null when the value is absent.
A human-readable context prefix for error messages, such as Tool 'x' arguments.
member.exception: Thrown when validation fails; the message names the failing path.

member.name: M:Voltaic.Mcp.McpSchemaValidator.CheckSchema(System.Object)
member.summary: Checks that a schema can be validated as written: its $schema dialect is supported (JSON Schema 2020-12, the default, or draft-07), it is well formed for that dialect (known keywords have values of the right type, type names are JSON Schema types, patterns are regular expressions, and subschemas are objects or booleans), and every $ref and $dynamicRef resolves within it. Unknown keywords are ignored. Returns a description of the first problem, or null when the schema is usable. Thread-safe.
member.param: The schema: a , a JSON string, or any serializable object.

member.name: T:Voltaic.Mcp.McpServer
member.summary: MCP server using stdio transport for subprocess-based operation. Implements Model Context Protocol stdio transport specification: newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin and stdout, nothing but MCP messages on stdout (while runs, is redirected to stderr so stray console output cannot corrupt the stream), requests handled concurrently so ping and notifications/cancelled take effect while other requests run, and the handshake-era initialization order enforced (requests other than initialize and ping before initialize get -32600). Requests whose _meta names 2026-07-28 are served statelessly.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpServer.ProtocolVersion
member.summary: Obsolete and has no effect. initialize must name a protocol version (a request without one gets -32602), so there is no version to fall back to; negotiation is capped by . The value is stored and returned for compatibility. Default is ; setting null restores the default.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpServer.IncludeToolExceptionMessages
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the message of an exception thrown by a tool handler is shown to the client. A handler exception becomes a tool result with isError set to true (a tool execution error the model can read). When false (the default), the text is a generic "Tool '<name>' failed because of an internal error." so internal details (connection strings, paths, host names) are not sent, as the MCP security considerations require tool outputs to be sanitized; when true, the text is "Tool '<name>' failed: <message>". The message of a is always shown, and the exception type and message are always written to the Log event. is sent as a JSON-RPC error instead.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpServer.MaximumHandshakeProtocolVersion
member.summary: Gets or sets the newest protocol revision the server agrees to during an initialize handshake. A client that requests a newer revision, or a stateless-era revision such as 2026-07-28 (which defines no initialize request and no sessions), is answered with this value, following the MCP rule that a server responds with a version it supports. Default is (currently 2025-11-25). Lower it to pin clients to an older revision. Setting null restores the default. Set this before the server starts accepting requests; it is not synchronized with in-flight handshakes.
member.exception: Thrown when the value is not a supported handshake-era revision (for example 2026-07-28 or an unknown version).

An update that follows the previous one sooner is not sent, except the final one (progress equal to the total). Default is 20. 0 sends every update. Maximum is 60000.

member.name: T:Voltaic.Mcp.McpTcpClient
member.summary:
Provides a TCP-based MCP (Model Context Protocol) client implementation for making remote procedure calls over a network. This class extends JsonRpcClient with MCP semantics:
Messages are newline-delimited JSON, the stdio framing MCP asks custom stream transports to reuse (set to false for Content-Length framing, which Voltaic TCP servers before 2.1.5 require).
Connecting performs the initialize handshake unless is false.
A ping from the server is answered with {}, other server requests by handlers registered with or with -32601.
A call that times out or is cancelled sends notifications/cancelled.

Must be a handshake-era revision (2024-11-05 through 2025-11-25), since a client must request a version it can negotiate. Default is . Setting null or whitespace restores the default.

member.name: T:Voltaic.Mcp.McpTcpServer
member.summary: Provides a TCP-based MCP (Model Context Protocol) server implementation for handling remote procedure calls over a network. This class extends JsonRpcServer with MCP-specific defaults and semantics.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpTcpServer.ProtocolVersion
member.summary: Obsolete and has no effect. initialize must name a protocol version (a request without one gets -32602), so there is no version to fall back to; negotiation is capped by . The value is stored and returned for compatibility. Default is ; setting null restores the default.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpTcpServer.IncludeToolExceptionMessages
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the message of an exception thrown by a tool handler is shown to the client. A handler exception becomes a tool result with isError set to true (a tool execution error the model can read). When false (the default), the text is a generic "Tool '<name>' failed because of an internal error." so internal details (connection strings, paths, host names) are not sent, as the MCP security considerations require tool outputs to be sanitized; when true, the text is "Tool '<name>' failed: <message>". The message of a is always shown, and the exception type and message are always written to the Log event. is sent as a JSON-RPC error instead.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpTcpServer.MaximumHandshakeProtocolVersion
member.summary: Gets or sets the newest protocol revision the server agrees to during an initialize handshake. A client that requests a newer revision, or a stateless-era revision such as 2026-07-28 (which defines no initialize request and no sessions), is answered with this value, following the MCP rule that a server responds with a version it supports. Default is (currently 2025-11-25). Lower it to pin clients to an older revision. Setting null restores the default. Set this before the server starts accepting requests; it is not synchronized with in-flight handshakes.
member.exception: Thrown when the value is not a supported handshake-era revision (for example 2026-07-28 or an unknown version).

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpTcpServer.ServerName

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpTcpServer.ServerVersion
member.summary: Gets or sets the server version for MCP serverInfo. Default is "1.0.0".

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpTcpServer.ServerInstructions
member.summary: Gets or sets optional natural-language instructions describing how to use the server, returned in the initialize result and by server/discover (2026-07-28). Null (the default) omits them.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpTcpServer.PageSize
member.summary: Gets or sets how many items one page of tools/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, or prompts/list returns before a nextCursor is issued. Default is 100. Minimum is 1.
member.exception: Thrown when the value is less than 1.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpTcpServer.ProgressIntervalMs
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum interval, in milliseconds, between progress notifications sent for one request (MCP: senders should rate-limit progress). An update that follows the previous one sooner is not sent, except the final one (progress equal to the total). Default is 20. 0 sends every update. Maximum is 60000.
member.exception: Thrown when set outside 0 to 60000.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpTcpServer.PingIntervalMs
member.summary: Gets or sets how often the server pings each client that completed initialize, in milliseconds, to check that the connection is healthy (MCP ping utility); a ping that is not answered within is logged. Default is 30000. 0 disables pinging. Maximum is 3600000.
member.exception: Thrown when set outside 0 to 3600000.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpTcpServer.PingTimeoutMs
member.summary: Gets or sets how long the server waits for a client to answer its ping, in milliseconds. Default is 10000. Minimum is 100; maximum is 600000.
member.exception: Thrown when set outside 100 to 600000.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpTcpServer.PingFailureThreshold
member.summary: Gets or sets how many consecutive pings a client may leave unanswered before the server treats the connection as failed and closes it (MCP: ping timeouts are connection failures). Default is 1. 0 only logs unanswered pings. Maximum is 100.
member.exception: Thrown when set outside 0 to 100.

member.name: T:Voltaic.Mcp.McpVersionCompatibility
member.summary: Downgrades server-produced MCP JSON (results, server notifications, and server capabilities) so it contains only what a handshake-era protocol revision (2024-11-05 through 2025-11-25) defines. Fields added in later revisions are removed and content block types that did not yet exist are converted to text blocks. Fields that exist in the target revision are never removed.
member.remarks: All methods mutate the supplied in place. They are no-ops for a null node, a node that is not a JSON object, an unknown protocol version, and the stateless 2026-07-28 revision. For 2025-11-25 only the stateless-era additions (resultType, ttlMs, cacheScope, and the extensions capability) are removed, because the 2025-11-25 schema does not define them. Thread safety: the class is stateless and safe to call concurrently, but callers must not mutate the same node from multiple threads at once.

The negotiated protocol version. Unknown versions and 2026-07-28 make this a no-op.

member.name: T:Voltaic.Mcp.McpVersionResolver
member.summary: Resolves the protocol version and era for an incoming MCP request using a deterministic precedence order. The resolver is transport-agnostic: it accepts the individual signals a transport can observe rather than a transport-specific request object, which makes it unit testable in isolation. All members are static and thread-safe.

member.name: M:Voltaic.Mcp.McpVersionResolver.Resolve(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Resolves the protocol version for a request from the available signals. Precedence, highest first:
The MCP-Protocol-Version header, when present.
The _meta protocol-version value carried in the request body.
Structural cues: an initialize method or a session header implies the handshake era; stateless routing headers imply the newest stateless revision.
With no signal at all, (2025-03-26), which the Streamable HTTP specification says a server assumes when a request carries no MCP-Protocol-Version header and nothing else identifies its version.
When both a header and a body _meta version are present and disagree, a with code -32020 (header mismatch) is thrown. When an explicitly requested version is unknown, a with code -32022 (unsupported protocol version) is thrown.
member.param: Value of the MCP-Protocol-Version header, or null.
Protocol version extracted from the request body _meta, or null.
The JSON-RPC method name, or null.
True when the request carries an Mcp-Session-Id header.
True when the request carries stateless routing headers (Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name).
member.returns: The resolved version and era. Never null.
member.exception: Thrown with code -32020 when header and body versions disagree, or with code -32022 when an explicitly requested version is unsupported.

member.name: M:Voltaic.Mcp.McpVersionResolver.ForVersion(System.String)
member.summary: Builds a resolved-version result for a known, supported version.
member.param: A supported protocol version string.
member.returns: The resolved version and era.
member.exception: Thrown when the version is not in the registry.

Requests the server sends to the client are always answered: ping with an empty result ({}), as the MCP specification requires of both parties, other methods by handlers registered with , and anything else with -32601 (method not found). member.summary: Registers the handler for requests the server sends to this client with the given method name (for example roots/list, sampling/createMessage, or elicitation/create), replacing any previous handler for that method. The handler receives the request parameters (null when the request has none) and a token that is cancelled when the client disconnects; its return value is sent as the result (null is sent as an empty object). A handler that throws sends that error; any other exception sends -32603 without its message. Requests for methods without a handler are answered with -32601. ping is always answered by the client itself. Handlers run concurrently with each other and with the receive loop. Thread-safe.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpWebsocketsServer.AuthenticationHandler
member.summary: Gets or sets an optional asynchronous authentication handler, the same delegate type as . It is invoked with the WebSocket upgrade request, so it can check Authorization, API-key headers, the query string, or client certificates. When it returns a result with false, the upgrade is refused with , (for example WWW-Authenticate), and . When it succeeds, the caller is stored in and is the ambient for every request on that socket, including the handler overloads. Default is null, which accepts every upgrade that passes the origin and loopback checks.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpWebsocketsServer.OriginPolicy
member.summary: Gets or sets the policy that decides which browser origins may open a socket. Browsers do not apply CORS to WebSockets, so this check is the defence against cross-site WebSocket hijacking. An upgrade whose Origin the policy rejects receives HTTP 403 before authentication. The default allows upgrades without an Origin header (non-browser clients) and loopback origins. Setting null restores the default policy.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpWebsocketsServer.RestrictToLoopbackClients
member.summary: Gets or sets whether only loopback clients are served. When true, an upgrade request whose remote address is not loopback receives HTTP 403. Default is true when the server is constructed with a loopback host name (localhost, 127.x.x.x, or ::1) and false otherwise. On Windows a localhost prefix is served on every interface and routed by the spoofable Host header, so this check is what keeps such a server local.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpWebsocketsServer.IncludeToolExceptionMessages
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the message of an exception thrown by a tool handler is shown to the client. A handler exception becomes a tool result with isError set to true (a tool execution error the model can read). When false (the default), the text is a generic "Tool '<name>' failed because of an internal error." so internal details (connection strings, paths, host names) are not sent, as the MCP security considerations require tool outputs to be sanitized; when true, the text is "Tool '<name>' failed: <message>". The message of a is always shown, and the exception type and message are always written to the Log event. is sent as a JSON-RPC error instead.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.McpWebsocketsServer.MaximumHandshakeProtocolVersion
member.summary: Gets or sets the newest protocol revision the server agrees to during an initialize handshake. A client that requests a newer revision, or a stateless-era revision such as 2026-07-28 (which defines no initialize request and no sessions), is answered with this value, following the MCP rule that a server responds with a version it supports. Default is (currently 2025-11-25). Lower it to pin clients to an older revision. Setting null restores the default. Set this before the server starts accepting requests; it is not synchronized with in-flight handshakes.
member.exception: Thrown when the value is not a supported handshake-era revision (for example 2026-07-28 or an unknown version).

member.summary: Sends notifications/progress for the in-flight request that carries . Called from a tool handler, the handler's own request is used; otherwise the notification is sent only when exactly one active request on any connection carries the token (tokens are unique only per client), and nothing is sent for a cancelled or finished request. Prefer , which is always scoped to the calling request.
member.param: Progress token from the request's _meta. Must not be null.
Current progress value. Must increase with every notification.
Optional total progress value.
Optional human-readable progress text.
Cancellation token.
member.returns: A task that represents the asynchronous operation.
member.exception: Thrown when is null.
Thrown when does not increase.

member.name: T:Voltaic.Mcp.SseSessionStreams
member.summary: The SSE streams of one Streamable HTTP session, so a client can resume a stream with Last-Event-ID. Only the most recent streams are kept. Streams are looked up within the session only, so an event ID from another session never replays anything. Thread-safe.

member.name: M:Voltaic.Mcp.SseSessionStreams.Open(System.String,System.Int32,System.Int64@)
member.summary: Returns the stream to write to. When names a retained stream of this session, that stream is resumed and is the sequence the client already has; otherwise a new stream is created and is -1.

member.name: T:Voltaic.Mcp.SseStreamLog
member.summary: The event history of one SSE stream in a Streamable HTTP session. Event IDs have the form {streamId}-{sequence}, so an ID names the stream it belongs to (as the MCP resumability rules require) and is unique across all streams of the session. The most recent capacity events are kept for replay. Thread-safe.

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.SseStreamLog.StreamId
member.summary: Gets the stream identifier (32 hexadecimal characters).

member.name: P:Voltaic.Mcp.SseStreamLog.CurrentEventId
member.summary: Gets the ID of the most recent event, or the stream's initial ID (sequence 0) before any event.

member.name: M:Voltaic.Mcp.SseStreamLog.Claim(System.Threading.CancellationTokenSource)
member.summary: Makes the connection that writes this stream and cancels the previous one. A client that resumes a stream has abandoned the old connection, whose loop would otherwise keep taking messages from the session queue until a write to the dead connection failed.

member.name: M:Voltaic.Mcp.SseStreamLog.Release(System.Threading.CancellationTokenSource)
member.summary: Clears the writer when it is still .

member.name: M:Voltaic.Mcp.SseStreamLog.Append(System.String,System.Threading.CancellationTokenSource)
member.summary: Records an event written by and returns it. When the writer is no longer the stream's owner (its client resumed the stream on a new connection while it was taking the message), the event is still recorded and the owner is woken so it sends the event itself.

member.name: M:Voltaic.Mcp.SseStreamLog.BeginWait(System.Int64)
member.summary: Returns a token the owner waits on alongside the session queue. It is cancelled when a former writer records an event, and is already cancelled when retained events newer than exist.

member.name: M:Voltaic.Mcp.SseStreamLog.After(System.Int64)
member.summary: Returns the retained events after the given sequence number, oldest first.
